args.text:
_Terre Haute, Indiana, September 6._

FRIEND AL: Well, Al old mate, I s'pose you seen it in the paper. They only gone and sold me to the White Sox! Fair dinkum Al it come as a surprise to me and I bet it did to all you good old mates back home too. You could of knocked me over with a feather when the old man come up to me and goes Jack, I've sold you to the Chicago Americans. Just like that, Al.

I had no bloody idea nothing like that was on the cards. For five whole minutes I was struck dum, standing there like a stunned mullet, couldn't get a word out.

Then he goes We aren't getting what you're worth, but I want you to get up to that big league and show them city fellas there's a Central League on the map. He goes Just pitch the ball you been pitching down here and it'll be easy as. And he goes All you need is a bit of ticker and Walsh or no one else won't have sweet bugger-all on you. Walsh, Al! Not a bad wrap, ay?

So I says I'd do me best and I thanked him for how they treated me in Terre Haute. They always looked after me here, and even though I carried more than me share of the load I always felt me work was appresiated. We're finishing second and I done most of it, if I say so meself. I can't help being proud of me first year in professional baseball, and you know I'm not skiting when I say that Al. Just telling it how it is.

Well Al it'll feel a bit funny being up there in the big show when I never been in a proper big city before. But I reckon I seen enough of life not to get spooked by a few tall buildings, ay Al? They're only buildings.

I'll just give 'em what I got, and if they don't like it they can send me back to the old Central and I'll be happy as Larry. No skin off my nose.

Now get this. I didn't have a clue anyone was having a squiz at me, but one of the boys tells me Jack Doyle, the White Sox scout, was down here watching me the whole time Grand Rapids was in town. Sneaky bugger. I beat 'em twice in that serious. You know Grand Rapids never had a hope against me when I was on song. I shut 'em out in the first game, and the only run they got in the second was cos Flynn misjuged that fly ball. Wasn't my fault, Al. Anyway Doyle liked what he seen and he wired Comiskey to buy me. Comiskey come back with an offer and they excepted it. I dunno how much they got for me, but whatever it was, I'm sold to the big league and believe me Al I'm gonna make good.

Well Al I'll be home in a few days and we'll have some of them beaut old times, just like before. Say g'day to all the boys and tell 'em I'm still their mate and I'm not getting up meself over this big league business. Not one bit.

Your mate, JACK.

A decent bloke; praise, not insult.

declined.reason: 'the old man' is the club boss; 'the old bloke' reads as any elderly man and loses that sense
'there won't be nothing to it' means it'll be easy; 'bugger all to it' isn't how it's said ('easy as' is)
'one of the boys' is a teammate, any age; 'young fellas' makes it about youngsters
